target_customer: Satellite manufacturers and operators, space station and orbital infrastructure builders that need large amounts of solar power per launch mass and volume
problem: Satellite power is limited by how large a solar array can fit in a launch vehicle and by structural vibration of long arrays; larger platforms such as orbital infrastructure need far more power.
business_model: Hardware sales of deployable solar arrays (Flarewing S, M and L) and thermal radiators, quoted per project
product_category: Deployable space solar arrays and radiators

founders.name: Mitchell Fogelson
prior_employers: NASA (design, simulation and optimization of deployable space structures)
founders.background_notes: YC page says he won the ASME JMD 2023 Editor's Choice Best Paper Award and invented the core technology.

founders.name: Pele Collins
prior_employers: SpaceX (parachute engineering and production, 30+ Dragon missions)
founders.background_notes: YC page gives both 6 and 7 years at SpaceX.

competitors.name: Redwire (ROSA roll-out solar arrays)
competitors.what: Roll-out solar arrays using composite booms as structure and deployment actuator
competitors.traction_then: More than 5 successful flight deployments per FY2023 10-K; 60 kW arrays tested for lunar Gateway in July 2025

technical_complexity.rationale: Space hardware with a novel deployable geometry must survive launch loads, deploy reliably in orbit and solve structural dynamics of very large arrays; first in-space demo is targeted for Q2 2027.

defensibility.rationale: Patented geometry, flight heritage requirements and long qualification cycles make fast copying hard, though Redwire has established roll-out arrays.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Redwire already flew roll-out arrays; no acquisition of Beyond Reach found.

market_need_then: Orbital infrastructure and data center concepts need far more power per launch; the company reports letters of intent from space companies totaling over $175M (company claim) and unveiled the Flarewing line in August 2026.

identity.voice_and_tone: Confident and forward looking; tagline Expansive innovation

branding.brand_signature: Flarewing product name and the football-field-in-orbit image
branding.community_and_virality: Coverage by SpaceNews, Payload and AlleyWatch in 2026 focused on the product and funding rather than the brand.

brand_strength.rationale: Product name Flarewing and the football-field framing travel well in trade press, but there is no evidence of community or brand driven growth.

outcome_analysis: Beyond Reach Labs raised a $10M seed in July 2026 after YC Winter 2026, opened a Brooklyn facility in September 2026 and unveiled Flarewing in August. Founders with NASA, SpaceX and deployable structure research backgrounds and a patented design support the technical moat, but flight proof is still ahead (demo targeted for Q2 2027).
notes: Seed amount and date from Payload; PitchBook and Dealroom headlines also show $10M. Total raised ranges from $10.5M to $325M across aggregators, where the larger numbers appear to count letters of intent, so they are ignored. The company site thanks NIAC, NASA, NSF and Innovation Works as supporters without amounts, not recorded as rounds. Payload and company sources differ on qualification milestones. Team size is 2 on one directory and 15 on the YC page. Prior to YC, a $500K figure appears on one aggregator and is unverified. Name origin unknown.
